title: Forward Engine Mount Bolt Bushing Standard on CVX-7200 Installations
abstract: Introduction of a shrink-fitted bushing at the forward engine mount bolt bores on CVX-7200 powered aircraft, after fretting was found at the bore surface during engine changes on high-utilisation airframes.

sections.reason: During routine engine changes, fretting marks and light bore ovality were reported at the forward mount bolt positions on twelve CVX-7200 powered aircraft, the earliest at 21 400 flight cycles. The bores are in a life-limited fitting that cannot be reworked in service beyond a shallow polish, so a finding beyond the polish limit means a pylon fitting change and a long downtime. The mechanism is micro-movement at the bolt-to-bore interface under the thrust reversal load case, which is more severe on this engine installation than on the Auran installation because of the mount geometry.
sections.description: A steel bushing is shrink-fitted into each forward mount bolt bore, giving a renewable wear surface between the bolt and the fitting. The upper bracket D7120112225413 is machined to the bushing interference fit and the forward bracket assembly D7120112258453 is replaced by an item with the same rework already applied. Titanium bolts LN569360-2A are retained at the mount and tension bolts AES840808-93 secure the revised heat shield bracket FAR360439-80. The obsolete upper heat shield CAD50991-63 is deleted, its function taken over by the revised bracket. The bushing is installed with the pylon fairing removed and the engine off the aircraft, in zones 441, 452 and 431. Bore preparation, bushing cooling and installation torques are given on drawing D71201124587. The heat shield FIN 4368PP is renewed at the same time; the mount shroud FIN 3879PP is refitted unchanged.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 2.4 kg per aircraft over four mount positions. No electrical load change. The bushed fitting is one-way interchangeable, since a bushed bore cannot be returned to the plain standard, but a bushed and an unbushed fitting may be carried on different pylons of the same aircraft. The benefit is that a future fretting finding is dealt with by changing the bushing rather than the fitting, which turns a pylon-level task into an engine-change-level one. Illustrated parts content for the mount and the engine change procedure both require update.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN T00163 in November 2019. In service the change is done at a scheduled engine removal, so no dedicated downtime is needed; the bushing installation itself takes about eleven hours per pylon. Kits are held as spares for use at overhaul.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric across four pylons, no reportable effect
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN T00163; bushing fitted at the pylon build station
